Fixture: H; a configuration K frozen at F (round branch from D on main) whose ledger carries edit e on path p; c0 = main at F's designation. f = an oi-review-record/1 file under verification/audits/r/ carrying a well-formed second-kind finding on e by an independent reviewer (verdict invalidates on

:scientific_effect, invalidated naming e, configuration naming K), reviewing reconciliation record q in the same directory. Unless stated, the run is op C execution with M = the last listed main commit and no REV. Unless a control changes that condition, q's side_change_commits meet R6.RECON.26's applicability condition at each named M. For an otherwise applying non-null repair, assume verifiable complete custody of its relevant historical inputs unless a control changes that condition. Proposed adjudication controls are conditional on an authorized admitted evidence route and confer no authority.

expected_vocabulary.outcome: FAIL, ERROR, PASS or ANY, as in EXPECTATIONS.json; ERROR means no verdict
expected_vocabulary.finding: the category3.findings element for f: present_at_M and witness (R6.OBL29.8); binding run-level where stated
expected_vocabulary.finding_references: number of distinct references carrying the finding
expected_vocabulary.invariants.finding_absent: the named reference and item do not appear in category3.findings
expected_vocabulary.invariants.finding_unblocked: the finding remains visible but has no corresponding category3.blocked element
expected_vocabulary.invariants.reassessment_applies: the named reassessment is present in category3.reassessments
expected_vocabulary.invariants.reassessment_absent: the named reassessment is absent from category3.reassessments
expected_vocabulary.invariants.record_invalid_for: a record-invalid item naming the specified discharge record or its defective review
expected_vocabulary.invariants.finding_observed: the exact reference and item appear in the emitted category3.findings
expected_vocabulary.invariants.admission_mode: the named ordinary chain or harness admission completed successfully and the result contains category3
expected_vocabulary.invariants.predecessor_review_checked: the named exact predecessor was resolved under the existing lineage anchor and its review was evaluated for this discharge
expected_vocabulary.invariants.predecessor_reference_unresol: the named exact predecessor was absent from the prescribed lineage anchor and could not be substituted from R*
expected_vocabulary.invariants.conflicting_successor: the exact successor and predecessor references are identified as ambiguous for an operative discharge
expected_vocabulary.invariants.live_REV_record_admitted: the named unrelated reconciliation record passes its own existing post-freeze admission
expected_vocabulary.invariants.qualified_witness_retained: independent replay verifies the exact original adverse evidence and its original scope, including any predecessor, repair and successor references
expected_vocabulary.invariants.custody_complete: verification establishes the custody starting point and relevant historical coverage, including authorized originating scopes and retained decisions
expected_vocabulary.invariants.verified_clearance: the substantive disposition is independently verified for the specified exact witness, with required authorization and positive admissibility
expected_vocabulary.invariants.clearance_history_retained: the original witness, original context, all reviewed corrections or adjudications, and their provenance remain available and verifiable
expected_vocabulary.invariants.reliance: the §2.2 reliance decision for the candidate discharge and the named retained witness: the witness class (lineage or review) and every matching clause (r1), (r2) or (r3), or none
expected_vocabulary.invariants.nonreliance_verified: the §2.2 clearance conditions for the witness class (NR-1 to NR-4 for a lineage witness; NR-1, NR-2, NR-4 and NR-5 for a review witness) hold for the named replacement record, decided from records and trees under the token rule

kinds.negative: a removal that must not lift the block
kinds.positive: a legitimate disappearance or a baseline that must behave as stated
kinds.countercase: an adversarial attempt to defeat the remedy
kinds.boundary: documents the edge of R* or the scope point of sec. 5.4
kinds.residual: documents a limit of the proposed walk, without implying owner acceptance

setup: Use one of the same-disputed-repair fixtures. Establish from complete custody that the original witness really qualified. Preserve the original finding, exact records, original configuration, review history and source objects.

Under the existing approved record route, tender a corrected replacement record R whose own lineage meets NR-1 and which F4 pins so that NR-2 holds. The accepting same-directory review of R's exact reference identifies the defect in the former basis in its method field, which also holds, as whole tokens under the §2.2 token rule, the git blob ids of the disputed record and of each witness record (NR-4). Build the required reviewed A2 and F4 with all ordinary current repair evidence.

Variant lineage witness: the witness is a qualified competing successor and the accepting review meets NR-3. Variant review witness: the witness is a qualifying adverse review or a failed required predecessor review, and the accepting review explicitly resolves it under NR-5, by that review's author. This variant keeps the requirement of a substantive review.

Verify that the replacement's linkage to the original adverse evidence and the chronological evidence remain available. Check that A2 applies and discharges the original finding only on the independently verified corrected basis.

controls.note: This tests the proposed semantics once an admitted evidence route is approved. Existing fields can carry the four elements of an explicit resolution, but no existing key or record kind carries the adjudicator's authorization, so this route is unavailable through existing records (§2.2 route 2). r8 gives no schema or automatic authority for an adjudication.

setup: Use the qualified dispute and preserved category-3 finding from N-REFREEZE-OPERATIVE-PIN-REMOVED. In each variant keep the otherwise applicable current repair entry and review.

Variant cosmetic: give the same repair new selector or supersession metadata or a renamed byte-identical record, without a reviewed correction linked to the original evidence. Variant unsupported correction: claim materially different repair evidence without independent verification of the former dispute and the new basis.

Variant adjudication: claim clearance through an unapproved input route, without independently reviewed substantive grounds, or with authorization or review for a different exact witness. Variant repeat: run the same frozen inputs again after an unresolved disposition.
Require the cited reassessment to remain inapplicable in each case. No variant may lose the original qualified witness or acquire new positive authority.
controls.note: The artifact can be a failed claim outside the configuration’s admitted inputs. An attempt to use an unrecognized configured record kind instead fails CONFIG_INVALID under the existing rules.

setup: Use N-REFREEZE-OPERATIVE-PIN-REMOVED with complete protected-main custody of the qualified S (competing with Q on exact P) under F2. Q is a multi-path reconciliation record (R6.RECON.1) with entries for p and for a second path p2. The F2 discharge used the entry for p.

Use a legitimately admitted F3 that removes Q's pin. Its reassessment A3 names the original f and item and cites Q's entry for p2. Variant same commits: the p2 entry lists the same exact repair commits as the p entry. Variant disjoint commits: the p2 entry lists repair commits disjoint from the p entry. In each variant every existing positive condition of R6.OBL29.4 holds at M, and the M-only lookup introduces no operative R6.REC.7 check. Run each variant twice with identical frozen inputs.

setup: Use the qualified S witness, Q, P, f and complete custody from N-REFREEZE-OTHER-ENTRY-SAME-Q. The witness is a lineage witness.

An accepting same-directory review of R's exact reference covers its items. Its reviewer differs, as identity strings, from the authors of R, A4, Q, P and S, from the reviewer of each review forming the witness and from the reviewer of every accepting review of Q. Under the §2.2 token rule its method holds the 40-hex git blob ids of Q and of S as whole tokens. No eligible review of R in R* dissents.

Use a legitimately admitted F4 that pins R through an existing route making R's R6.REC.6 and R6.REC.7 checks operative. Those checks pass on their prescribed inputs and on R*. Its reviewed reassessment A4 names f and item and cites R's entry for p, with every ordinary current repair input present at M.

controls.note: Clearance follows from NR-1 to NR-4, read from records and trees. NR-4 uses the existing method field and needs no schema change. N-REFREEZE-NONRELIANCE-UNSUPPORTED removes or forges each element of this evidence.

setup: Start from P-REFREEZE-INDEPENDENT-REPLACEMENT and change one element per variant, keeping every other input.

Variant self-reviewed: R's only accepting review is by the author of R, A4, Q, P or S, or by the author of Q's original accepting review. Variant forged: non-reliance is asserted only in R's own text, in A4, in F4, in a commit message or in pull request text, or the accepting review names a different exact reference, lies outside R's reconciliation directory or omits an item.

Variant unlinked: R's own text and the reassessment name Q's and S's git blob ids, but the accepting review's method gives only their paths, abbreviated ids, upper-case ids or SHA-256 values, joins an id to adjacent punctuation such as a trailing comma, or omits S's blob id.

Variant chain: F4 pins R2, which names R1 in supersedes, and R1, distinct from Q, names P. Variant dissent: an eligible review of R in R* dissents and is later deleted.

invariants.reliance: lineage witness against Q; (r2) in variant through-Q, otherwise (r3) only with NR-1 failing in variants shared predecessor and chain, NR-4 in variant unlinked, and another of NR-1 to NR-4 in the remaining variants

controls.note: Non-reliance fails closed. A required object that is unreadable or does not hash to its id is ERROR instead, as in B-CUSTODY-MISSING-REQUIRED-OBJECT. No variant supplies positive authority.

setup:
Variant direct: the witness is a qualifying adverse review V of Q by reviewer v, with a reject verdict on item

:scientific_effect, qualified under F2 and in complete custody. Variant predecessor: the witness is the eligible dissent of P from variant Q of N-OPERATIVE-PREDECESSOR-DISSENT-DELETED, which failed Q's required predecessor check under F2.

Variant substitution: Q' has an accepting same-directory review by a fresh reviewer whose author login differs from all those NR-3 excludes, carrying every token NR-4 and NR-5 would require and non-empty reasons. Variant general accept: the only accepting review of Q' is by the adverse reviewer, with every item accepted but without the <b>#<item> token for the adverse item or the token for f, or with empty reasons on the cited entry's items.

Variant wrong item: the adverse reviewer's review of Q' carries a <b>#<item> token for a different item of V, or names V's SHA-256 or path instead of its git blob id. Variant wrong replacement: the adverse reviewer's fully tokened review names a different exact reference than the record A3's repair.entry cites. Run each variant twice with identical frozen inputs.

Under the §2.2 token rule Z's method holds the git blob ids of Q and of the review forming the witness, the token # for each adverse item of that review, and the token # for f, where is the git blob id of f's file. Z accepts every item of R. Its reasons on R's items

and
